colors.name: ground
colors.role: background — warm white, the desk the stickers sit on; never pure white (ink holds 16.5:1 on it, AAA)

colors.name: ink
colors.role: the chunky outline and all functional text — every sticker's border, label text, focus ring. Ink-on-sticker is the universal AA pattern: 6.7:1 on tangerine, 9.0:1 on sky, 10.7:1 on lime, 5.0:1 on grape (all pass)

colors.name: tangerine
colors.role: the lead sticker color and brand accent — wordmark fill, hero CTA, marquee row B. 2.5:1 on ground so DISPLAY/SURFACE only; carries ink text at 6.7:1

colors.name: tangerine-deep
colors.role: where the accent must function as TEXT on ground — eyebrows, the section-number stamps, focus-ring accent. 4.96:1 on ground (AA)

colors.name: sky
colors.role: sticker color — the playful second voice, the parallax far-layer fill, ::selection ground. Carries ink text at 9.0:1

colors.name: lime
colors.role: sticker color — the energy note, the READY/초록 stamp. Carries ink text at 10.7:1 (AAA)

colors.name: grape
colors.role: sticker color — the cool counterweight, the 'after hours' voice, marquee row A accents. Carries ink text at 5.0:1 (AA)

colors.name: lemon
colors.role: sticker color — highlight bursts, the star rating, the ! in pop. Carries ink text at 12.6:1 (AAA)

colors.name: bubble
colors.role: sticker color — the pink candy note, hearts, the 비밀 secret stamp. Carries ink text at 6.1:1 (AA)

colors.name: paper
colors.role: the paper backing of white sticker decals (note-paper, barcode) — pure white against the warm ground reads as a peel-off sticker

fonts.role: Korean display — the wordmark 스티커, section titles, the giant footer shout. The webtoon-cover voice: loud, rounded, impossible to ignore. Hangul glyphs ride the font's own CJK coverage (subsets: latin)
everyday Korean — captions, sticker labels, the notebook-hand voice. A handwritten rounded face so every line feels ballpoint-on-sticker, not set in a system font
English voice — the wordmark subtitle, English labels, marquee slogans. Rounded sans, warm and chunky, the way a sticker book is printed

texture: Three static layers, none animated (a sticker is a physical object; it does not shimmer). (1) Paper warmth: one fixed full-viewport SVG feTurbulence (fractalNoise, baseFrequency 0.9, 2 octaves, seed 3, stitchTiles) mapped by feColorMatrix to ink at ~5% alpha, mix-blend-mode: multiply, opacity 0.5 — the warm-white desk is paper, not screen. (2) Dotted grid: a faint repeating-radial dot field (rgba(26,26,26,0.05), 1.5px dots every 28px) — the peel-and-stick backing sheet every sticker is die-cut from. (3) Physical depth: every sticker carries an offset solid drop-shadow (0 5px 0 rgba(26,26,26,0.18) at rest, 0 11px 0 rgba(26,26,26,0.22) while grabbed) plus a 3px ink outline — zero blur, because a sticker casts a hard shadow, not a haze.

motion.name: spring-stiffness
motion.value: 0.14 — the spring constant for a released sticker; tuned so a fling settles in ~620ms with two visible bounces

motion.name: spring-damping
motion.value: 0.78 — critical-ish; enough overshoot to feel bouncy, not enough to oscillate forever

motion.name: fling-friction
motion.value: 0.92 per 60fps-normalized frame — initial momentum glide before the spring takes over (~250ms handoff)

motion.name: grab-torque
motion.value: vr += 0.5 × (vx·−gy + vy·gx) — release velocity crossed with grab offset; grab a corner and it spins

motion.name: pile-nudge
motion.value: released sticker pushes resting neighbors within 1.1× combined radius by 0.35 of its overlap — they settle into a pile, not a stack

motion.name: parallax-depth
motion.value: hero layers translate by pointer offset × {back 0.04, mid 0.08, front 0.14, stickers 0.20}, lerped by 1−0.82^(dt/16.7), capped ±18px

motion.name: marquee-base
motion.value: 0.05 px/ms (~50 px/s) each row, opposite directions; sign flips with scroll direction

motion.name: marquee-boost
motion.value: +0.05 px/ms per unit of smoothed scroll velocity, capped 0.30 px/ms; approach by 1−0.86^(dt/16.7) so a flip skids

motion.name: wobble
motion.value: resting stickers sway ±1.2deg over a 4–6s loop, mutually prime per sticker — the page breathes like things left on a desk

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: sections rise translateY(24px)→0 + opacity 0→1 over 700ms ease-back (cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1)) with 90ms stagger — a sticker being peeled up

motion.name: press
motion.value: scale(0.94) on :active, 120ms cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) snap-back — a sticker squished under a thumb
